lessons.title: Skid Control and Recovery

content.text: A skid happens when the vehicle’s wheel slides out of control on a slippery surface. Skids can involve the front, rear or all four wheels. Even careful drivers experience skids. You lose traction and your wheels spin or lock, usually when braking, turning or accelerating.

keyPoints: A skid happens when the vehicle’s wheel slides out of control on a slippery surface.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of this section on 'Skid Control and Recovery'?
options: Understanding skid control and recovery concepts and safe practices

lessons.title: Causes of Skids:

items: Driving faster than the road or traffic conditions allow
Turning too fast or accelerating too quickly.

keyPoints: Driving faster than the road or traffic conditions allow
Turning too fast or accelerating too quickly.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of this section on 'Causes of Skids:'?
options: Understanding skid control and recovery concepts and safe practices

lessons.title: The Front Wheel Skid

content.text: This happens when the vehicle goes off the intended course. It is caused by excess speed on entry at a corner or a bend.  It also occurs during sudden braking when negotiating a hazard.

keyPoints: This happens when the vehicle goes off the intended course.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of this section on 'The Front Wheel Skid'?
options: Understanding skid control and recovery concepts and safe practices

lessons.title: The Rear Wheel Skid

content.text: This occurs when the rear of the vehicle swings out of the line as if the vehicle is trying to overtake at the front. It is often caused excessive speed leading to sudden braking in a hazard situation.

keyPoints: This occurs when the rear of the vehicle swings out of the line as if the vehicle is trying to overtake at the front.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of this section on 'The Rear Wheel Skid'?
options: Understanding skid control and recovery concepts and safe practices

lessons.title: Aquaplaning

content.text: Driving too fast or at an excessive or inappropriate speed on a wet road causes aquaplaning. When the tyre tread cannot channel away enough water, the tyre(s) lose contact with the road and the vehicle floats on a wedge of water. Aquaplaning can be avoided by reducing speed in wet conditions. Having the correct tyre pressure and tyre tread depth will maximise your tyres’ ability to maintain their road grip. If it happens, ease off the accelerator and brakes until your speed drops sufficiently for the car tyres to make contact with the road again

keyPoints: Driving too fast or at an excessive or inappropriate speed on a wet road causes aquaplaning.

lessons.title: Skid recovery

items: Take your feet off the accelerator pedals
Release the brake pedal and reapply the brakes gently
Quickly turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go
As your vehicle turns back in the correct direction, you may then need to steer in the opposite direction so as to stay on your desired path
Continue to look at your path of travel down the road

keyPoints: Take your feet off the accelerator pedals
Release the brake pedal and reapply the brakes gently
Quickly turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go

quiz.question: The most common cause of skidding is:
options: Driving too fast for road conditions

quiz.question: If your rear wheels skid to the right, you should steer:
options: Right (into the direction of the skid)

quiz.question: Aquaplaning occurs when:
options: A layer of water prevents tyre contact with the road
The road is covered with gravel

quiz.question: To recover from a skid you should:
options: Steer in the direction you want to go and ease off the throttle
Turn the wheel sharply in the opposite direction

quiz.question: A front-wheel skid is typically caused by:
options: Braking too hard causing the front wheels to lock
